post.description:
The app asks its sidecar to stop (at quit, or to replace it).

Needs the launch secret like every other route (ADR 0002): a web
page that can reach the port must not be able to stop it. The
answer goes out first; open requests then get
`lifecycle.GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN_S` and the process exits.

get.description:
Server-sent stream of changes to shared state.

The renderer holds one of these open for the life of the window.
It exists because the window is no longer the only writer: a model
connected over MCP edits the same Workbench, and without this
the window would keep showing a stale draft and then autosave it
back over the model's work.

Events are hints — `{event, at, ...ids}`. The renderer re-reads
through the normal endpoints when one arrives.

What the MCP endpoints are and how many tools each carries.

Powers Settings → MCP. Deliberately *not* under /mcp — that prefix
belongs to the protocol itself, and this is a plain REST read for
the renderer.

post.description:
Issue a bearer token for the MCP endpoints, replacing any
existing one. Clients using the old token stop working.

Off by default — see `services/mcp_auth.py` for why. The token is
returned once here and again from `/mcp-info`, because the user has
to be able to copy it into a client config at any point.

delete.description: Turn the MCP bearer requirement back off.

get.description:
Search the cached eicon catalog (sourced from xariah.net).

The renderer uses this to populate the toolbar's eicon picker. The
catalog is loaded into memory at sidecar startup with delta refreshes
every hour. While the first fetch is in flight `status` will be
'loading'; the renderer should poll or show a spinner.

Public profile fetch routed through the F-list JSON API.

Replaces the previous HTML scrape (`flist.fetch_profile`). The shape
returned here matches the old `Profile.to_dict()` so existing
renderer code in EditorPane's "Fetch profile" button still works
against it. Requires an active sign-in — 401 surfaces a "Sign in to
F-list first" CTA in the renderer.

Footer chip polls this every 60s for session age + hourly count.
Stateless — never refreshes the ticket on its own; refresh happens
on the next ticket-requiring action.

Also reports `password_idle_seconds_remaining` so the renderer can
surface a "session will be cleared in Nm" warning before the
watchdog drops the cached password (UX gap from the 2026-05-30 QA
verification of P0-C).

post.description:
Trade (account, password) for an F-list session ticket.

The ticket is held in sidecar RAM only (`flist_api.TicketStore`).
The password is held too — see flist_api docstring for why — but
neither value crosses this endpoint boundary. Renderer gets back
the character list and an expiry hint.

Schedules a fire-and-forget avatar warm-up for every account
character so the picker has avatars ready by the time the user
opens it (instead of waiting for 30+ lazy fetches to serialise
through the CDN rate limiter).

Explicit re-trigger of the avatar warm-up.

Useful if a sign-in race left some avatars un-cached, or if F-list
avatars changed on the user's side and we want to refresh the whole
set. Fires immediately, returns the scheduled count, downloads
happen in the background.

get.description:
In-memory append-only audit log of F-list operations (sign-in,
ticket refresh, per-character pull stages, idle password clear,
sign-out). Closes the trust-question gap surfaced by the
2026-05-30 UX subagent review — see UX F4 in
REVIEW_2026-05-30_post_tier1_polish.md.

Roster union: account roster (if signed in) + archived characters
+ characters with local F-Chat logs. Each entry carries flags so the
picker can render status badges.

Serve a cached avatar from `<userdata>/avatars/`. Fetches on
miss; avatars are public so this works signed-out too.

F-list returns a 5827-byte placeholder PNG (HTTP 200) for any name
without an uploaded avatar — there's no 404 path. We detect that
by size and surface a real 404 so the renderer's `onError` fires
and the initial-circle fallback renders instead of an alien
placeholder graphic.

200.description: The avatar F-list has for the character.

post.description:
Pull live character data + images for `name`, as a job.

Answers with the job's progress as an SSE stream (`sse.follow`),
or with `wait=false` the job itself (202), to follow later through
`/jobs/{id}/events`. Closing the stream leaves the Pull running;
`DELETE /jobs/{id}` cancels it. 409 `character_busy` while another
job holds the character. The work lives in `services/pull.py`, so
the MCP `pull_character` tool runs exactly the same job; event
names and payloads are documented there.

200.description: The job, then its progress events until it ends.

post.description:
A manual Backup: pack the character's Workbench into a
userscript-restoreable ZIP at `backups/<ISO>.zip`, recorded as
`source: workbench, occasion: manual`, so the user can park their
work. Live needs no manual Backup: Back up all and every Upload keep
it.

`force=True` is the default because the explicit right-click asked
for an artefact in hand and dedup would be surprising. A `kind`
query parameter, which older windows sent, is ignored.

schema.title: Response Flist Character Zip Backup Flist Character  Character Id  Zip Backup Post

delete.description:
Move a single Backup to the character's Trash, user-set name and
all; it can be restored from there until the Trash is emptied.
Filename validated against the ISO-basic format so a crafted `../`
path moves nothing. 404 if the Backup isn't there.

patch.description:
Rename a single backup. The ZIP file itself isn't modified;
the user-set name lives in a sidecar `_names.json` map next to
the ZIPs. Empty-string name clears the entry (so the UI falls
back to the timestamp-derived default). Returns the canonical
entry for the renamed backup so the renderer can update its
in-memory list without a separate /zip-backups re-fetch.

get.description:
Stream the raw ZIP bytes for a saved backup. Used by Sidebar
→ Backups → right-click → Download ZIP… so the user can lift a
backup off the machine without digging into %APPDATA%. Filename
parsing must match the ISO-basic backup filename format; we
reject anything else so this endpoint can't be turned into an
arbitrary-file-read by crafting a `../` path.

200.description: The Backup's zip, as it is on disk.

get.description:
Read the embedded working.json out of a ZIP backup for the
read-only Browse Backup mode.

Backups created since 2026-06-17 (the day this endpoint shipped)
bundle a `working.json` file alongside the userscript-targeted
`character.json`. We read the former so the renderer's editor
tabs can render the rich internal shape (descriptions, kink
overlay, custom-kink dict, etc.) without inverting the export
reshape passes.

Older backups predate the `working.json` write and answer 409
`backup_too_old`, as Restore does. We deliberately don't try to invert
character.json on the fly; it's a multi-stage lossy reshape and
not worth the complexity for the v1 ship.

post.description:
Back up every character on the signed-in account, as a job.

Answers like a Pull (`flist_character_pull`): the progress stream,
or with `wait=false` the job. One Back up all at a time, and none
while a Pull runs (409 `character_busy`). The sweep lives in
`services/backup_all.py` so the MCP `backup_all_characters` tool
runs the same one; event names and payloads are documented there.

200.description: The job, then its progress events until it ends.

get.description:
The character's one editable copy, created from Live if needed:
`{workbench: {name, created_at, updated_at}}`.

`create=false` answers "is there one yet" without making it so,
which is what a read-only render wants.

schema.title: Response Flist Character Workbench Flist Character  Character Id  Workbench Get

get.description:
The Workbench payload and the etag a save must send back.

Made from Live when the character has none yet, and then `created`
says so: that copy holds nobody's edits. `create=false` reads
without making one (404 `no_workbench`).

put.description:
Save the whole Workbench, against the etag the caller read.

No `If-Match` is a write by something that never read what it is
replacing: refused with 409 `etag_required`, like a stale etag
(409 `etag_mismatch`). A window that had seeded its editor from
Live once flattened a long draft down to the published text this
way, one keystroke at a time. Both carry the current etag.

post.description:
Restore: replace the Workbench contents with a Backup's.

The Workbench it replaces is saved as a `before-restore` Backup
first, always; `backed_up_first` names it (null when there was no
Workbench yet). When that Backup cannot be written, nothing is
replaced and the caller hears 500 `workbench_not_kept`.

`live_diverged` is reported back rather than enforced. A backup can
be older than the profile now on F-list, and loading it anyway is a
legitimate thing to want — the window says so and lets the user
decide.

post.summary: Flist Character Workbench Reset To Live
post.description:
Reset to Live: the Workbench becomes a fresh copy of Live.

Done here rather than in the window so the Workbench it replaces is
saved as a `before-restore` Backup first, whoever asks; that Backup
is `backed_up_first` (null when there was no Workbench yet). When it
cannot be written nothing is replaced: 500 `workbench_not_kept`. A
character never pulled has no Live: 404 `no_live`.

Answers with the new payload and its etag, which the window adopts
as the Workbench it saves over next.

get.description:
What the confirm dialog needs to say before overwriting the bench.

Answers two questions the user cannot see for themselves: whether
the bench currently holds anything that is not already in Live, and
whether F-list has moved on since the backup was taken.

Serve `images/<image_id>.<ext>`. The filename shape is validated
against the safe-name regex so a hostile renderer call can't path-
traverse out of the images directory.

200.description: An image file in the Pool.

get.description:
List the files in `images/`. Each row: `{image_id, extension,
size, added_at}`. Renderer pairs these with description/sort_order
from the Workbench to decide which are on the profile vs. in the
Pool view.

post.description:
Upload an image into `images/` under a `local-<sha8>` synthetic
id. The body is the raw image bytes; the server sniffs magic bytes
to decide the extension (Content-Type is never trusted). The
uploaded image lands in the renderer's Pool view by default — it
only appears on-profile after the user moves it via a Workbench
gallery edit.

Idempotent — identical bytes always produce the same `local-<sha8>`
id and skip re-writing the file.

get.description:
Serve `images/<image_id>.<ext>` without the renderer having to
know the extension. Tries the supported set in order; 404 when none
exists. Lets the gallery render thumbnails reliably without a
separate round-trip to look up extensions.

200.description: The Pool's image file of that id.

post.description:
Put the gallery back together when entries have lost their bytes.

Called when the Images tab opens. A slot pointing at a file that is
gone renders as a black placeholder, and — worse — drops out of the
restore ZIP, which the extension reads as "delete this from the
profile". Users lost images on f-list.net that way, so this runs on
its own rather than waiting to be found in a menu.

Cheap: it hashes the character's own image files and nothing else.

delete.description:
Delete one image: off the Workbench's gallery if it is there,
and into the character's Trash, where it can be restored until the
Trash is emptied. The same as the batch route below.

post.description:
Delete images, whether in the gallery or only in the Pool: the
window's delete, and the same function MCP's `trash_images` calls.
A gallery image is taken off the Workbench's gallery first; the
answer's `etag` is the Workbench's new one (None when the gallery
was left alone), which the window saves its next edit over.

get.description:
Where each image id is still used — the Workbench, Live and
Backups — so the window can warn before trashing one.

delete.description: Empty the whole Trash: images, Backups and cleared Labels.

get.description: Serve a trashed file, for the trash view's thumbnails.

200.description: An image file in the Trash.

post.description: Put trashed files back into the Pool (not onto the profile).

post.summary: Flist Character Trash Backups Put Back
post.description: Put trashed Backups back in the Backup list, under their names.

post.summary: Flist Character Trash Labels Put Back
post.description:
Put cleared Labels back. A message labelled again since keeps
its newer Label and is reported under `skipped`.

200.description: An inline image file of the profile.

get.description:
Every cleared-Labels entry in the Trash, newest first, for
Settings → Labels. Unlike a character's Trash view this includes a
Log character with no Workbench, and one whose Log name matches no
character in the list.

post.description:
Put cleared Labels back, whichever character they were cleared
for. A message labelled again since keeps its newer Label and is
reported under `skipped`.

Delete cleared Labels for good. The window's call only: MCP has
no tool for it.

get.description:
Build the userscript-compatible Upload ZIP (Tier 6).

Bundles `character.json` + every image referenced by the
Workbench's gallery + the avatar. The renderer triggers a
download by navigating to this URL, so the response stamps a
`Content-Disposition: attachment` with a filename derived from
the character name.

The export modal shows the Workbench's counts, so this is the
Workbench too: what the user reviewed is what they upload. Live is
the fallback only for a character that has no Workbench yet.

200.description: The Upload ZIP, as an attachment.

Response Handshake Reject Restore Handshake Reject Post

get.description:
Whether the browser extension is paired, for Settings → Security.

Outside `/restore/` on purpose: it answers the app window only
(launch secret), never the extension, and never returns the token.

Which extension version the browser is running, as of its last
authenticated call. `version` is null until it has made one.

schema.title: Response Upload Characters Restore Characters Get
Response Upload Sources Restore Snapshots Get

get.description:
One Upload source as a ZIP; `snapshot_id` is the id the source
list gave it.

schema.title: Response Pre Upload Backup Restore Snapshot Fresh Post

post.description:
The extension reporting what F-list called our uploads — noted, not applied.

An image uploaded in the app is keyed by a hash of its bytes, because
it has no F-list id until someone uploads it. The extension learns
the real id at that moment and used to hand it over here, with the
archive renaming files and rewriting set payloads on the spot.

It no longer acts on that report. The upload happens during Import —
before the user has pressed Save, before F-list's profile actually
contains the picture. Renaming local files for an id the profile may
never get turned uploads into dangling gallery rows and vanished
images: the rename had already destroyed the only copy of the bytes,
and a subsequent pull (which reflects the real profile) had nothing
left to fold back in.

The same folding still happens — at the moment it is true. A saved
profile re-pulls; `dedupe_local_after_pull` matches each pulled
image's bytes against the local upload and moves the gallery over to
the real id then, and `collapse_local_duplicates` catches any pair
that ended up side by side on disk when the Images tab lists them.
Same cure, applied when the diagnosis holds.

The user pressed Save on f-list.net — re-pull so Live matches
what is published again.

Live is the only thing this touches. The pull writes live.json and
the images; the Workbench must come through untouched: the user
may well have gone on editing it while the upload happened, and
quietly replacing their draft with what they just published would
be the rudest possible interpretation of "the Upload finished".

Returns immediately. A pull takes seconds and the extension has a
page to get on with; it is fire-and-forget by design, and the
renderer hears about the result over the event stream like any
other pull. The Pull is a job like any other once it starts
(`services.pull.start_when_free`): after `delay_seconds`, and
after any Pull or Back up all that holds the character then has
finished. It holds nothing while it waits, so a Pull the user
starts in the window meanwhile is not refused.

get.description:
Candidate names from one of the viewer's three sources.

`bookmarks` and `friends` come off the F-list account (one API
call, memoised); `logs` walks the local F-Chat log directories and
costs nothing; `name` echoes the typed string back because F-list
has no character search to call.

How much disk the Foreign profile cache takes: `{bytes,
profiles, cap_bytes}`.

delete.description:
Delete every cached Foreign profile, images and avatars included.
Not the Trash: these are copies of other people's profiles.

get.description:
One foreign profile. Served from cache while it is under the
24-hour TTL; `refresh=true` is the viewer's reload button.

The profile's avatar, cached inside its own foreign folder.

Kept out of `<userdata>/avatars/`, which the account picker treats
as "characters this user has". Same placeholder detection as
`/flist/avatar/{name}` so the renderer falls back to an initial
circle instead of showing F-list's grey stand-in.

After a refresh of the profile the avatar is fetched again; the old
one is served until the new one has arrived.

200.description: The avatar of the Foreign profile.

get.description:
A gallery image, downloaded on first request and cached after.

Lazy on purpose: a profile can list fifty images and fetching the
set up front would turn opening a profile into a half-minute
wait. The id must appear in the cached profile's own gallery —
that is what stops this route being a general-purpose proxy for
anything on the CDN.

200.description: A gallery image of the Foreign profile.

schema.title: Response Logs Search All Logs Search All Get

get.description:
The app's long-poll for something to draw.

Answering this is also how the app says "I am here": a tool asking
for a picture checks that before it waits, so a model gets told the
window is closed instead of sitting through a timeout.

post.description: The finished PNG, straight from the app's offscreen capture.

The app could not draw this one — say why rather than let the
caller sit out the timeout.

get.description:
Batch labels stats for every partner of a character.

The sidebar uses this to render per-partner coverage pips without
firing one request per row. Reuses the same counts as
/labels/stats so a partner's per-row counts always match the
detailed view. Linked aliases are folded into their primary partner.

Each row also returns `log_mtime` (latest of all alias-group log
files) and `last_label_at` (newest labels.updated_at across the
same alias group). A stale partner is one where log_mtime >
last_label_at — log activity arrived after the last classify run
for that conversation.

post.description:
Delete every label (LLM + manual) for one conversation.

Used by the renderer's "Reset all labels" context-menu action.
After this returns, the resolver falls back to rule-on-read for
every message in that conversation. The cleared Labels go to the
character's Trash first (`trash_id`), where Restore puts them back.

Wipe every stored IC/OOC verdict across all characters.

The Settings → Labels "Reset all labels…" button calls this. After
it returns, every message in every conversation falls back to
rule-on-read — manual overrides are gone too. The cleared Labels go
to the Trash first, one entry per character whose Logs hold the
messages and one, with no character, for messages in none of the
Logs; the renderer still confirms before invoking this.

get.description:
Aggregate IC/OOC/Unlabeled counts across every character.

Walks every (character × partner) log under the configured data
directory; for large corpora this is a few seconds the first time
Settings opens. Used by the Labels rollup pane to show one-glance
state ("3,402 IC · 18,720 OOC · …").

post.description:
Give every still-Unlabeled message in one conversation the same
verdict.

For a conversation the user knows is pure IC (or pure OOC) end to
end. Walking it batch by batch through a connected model buys
nothing when they already know the answer.

Deliberately narrow: messages that already carry a verdict keep it,
and messages the rules decide keep resolving through the rules. So
this can add labels but never overwrite a model's or the user's
own. The response carries every hash written, which is what makes
the undo exact.

Remove named labels and nothing else — the undo for
`/labels/fill-unlabeled`. Distinct from `/labels/clear`, which
drops every verdict in the conversation including a model's.

schema.title: Response Labels Override Labels Override Post

post.description:
`/labels/override` for the log view's multi-select: one verdict,
or a reset, for any set of messages in one conversation.

One canned embedding — validates that the model loads and says
what dimension it produces.

Returns latency + dimension on success; ok=false + structured
error string on failure. Same 200-always shape as
/labels/test-connection so the UI can render either with one path.

Drop the local Qdrant collection and clear the manifest.

Pure delete — no re-ingest, no probe. Use this when you want to
forget everything and rebuild on your own schedule (e.g. after
changing chunking settings without immediately re-embedding 80k
messages). The next /rag/ingest starts cold. Refused with
`index_busy` while an ingest runs.

Rebuild the BM25 lexical index from the existing Qdrant chunks.

Avoids a full re-ingest when the dense store is up-to-date but the
lexical mirror is stale (e.g. after a chunking-config change that
only required re-embedding once, or after upgrading from a pre-
hybrid install). Returns the number of chunks indexed.

get.description:
Snapshot of the local vector store + manifest.

Used by the renderer's Settings → RAG panel to show "indexed: N
chunks for model X (dim 768)". Cheap — one Qdrant count + one SQLite
read. While an ingest runs it says `busy` and names the job instead
of counting.

delete.description:
Ask a job to stop; it stops where it next checks. Answers the
job as it stands, with `cancel_requested` set unless it had already
finished.

get.description:
Follow a Pull or Back up all as server-sent events: the `job`,
every event it has sent so far, then each new one until it ends.
How a reopened progress view picks up a running job; closing the
stream leaves the job running.

200.description: A Pull's or Back up all's events: first `job` (the job as `GET /jobs/{job_id}` answers it), then each event it sent and sends, ending with `done`, `error` (`{stage, code, message, details}`) or `cancelled`.

get.description:
Return {primary_name: [member names…]} for one character.

Empty dict when the character has no linked partners. Renderer
uses this to decide whether to render alias hints on each partner
row.

delete.description: Drop one name from its alias group.
Drop every member of an alias group at once.

post.description:
The embedding models that can be selected.

This used to enumerate whatever an inference server had loaded.
Embedding runs in-process now, so the honest answer is fastembed's
own catalogue — with the dimension, download size and licence, since
those are what the choice actually turns on. Licence matters:
the catalogue mixes apache-2.0 and MIT with cc-by-nc-4.0.

of the bytes), with the newest of them. `migration_backup`: the
older copies from before the upgrade name it; that Backup holds
JSON only, no copy of the bytes, and is not counted in `backups`.

ImageReferences.title: ImageReferences
ImageReferences.description: Every image id mentioned anywhere, and where.

ImageStats.description: A character's images after its Pull, by outcome.
ImageStats.title: ImageStats

ImagesDeleted.title: ImagesDeleted
ImagesDeleted.description:
Images deleted: their files went to the Trash (`trashed`), and
those the Workbench's gallery showed came off it (`off_gallery`).
`etag` is the Workbench's new one; null when the gallery was left
alone.

IndexStatus.title: IndexStatus
IndexStatus.description:
What the Index holds: model, dimension, last ingest, chunk
count. While a job holds the Index, `busy` and that `job` instead,
and `chunk_count` is null because the Index can't be counted.

IngestFailedDay.title: IngestFailedDay
IngestFailedDay.description: A day whose chunks did not reach both halves of the Index.

IngestJob.title: IngestJob
IngestJob.description:
An ingest as a job: a `Job` whose params, progress and result
are the ingest's.

IngestProgress.title: IngestProgress
IngestProgress.description:
What an ingest has done so far (`rag_jobs.IngestProgress`).
`skipped_unlabeled`: messages left out for lack of an IC/OOC
verdict; a high count means the classification flow should run
first.

IngestScope.title: IngestScope
IngestScope.description:
What an ingest covers: every Log (`{}`), every conversation of
one character, or one conversation.

Job.title: Job
Job.description:
Long work the sidecar runs as a job, of any kind
(`services.jobs`): started by its own route, then polled and
cancelled by id (`/jobs/{id}`). `params`, `progress` and `result`
are the kind's own; `error` is set when it failed.

JobCancelled.description:
A stream's `cancelled` event: a cancel by job id stopped the
job. No data.
JobCancelled.title: JobCancelled

JobError.title: JobError
JobError.description:
Why a job failed, in the one error shape `{code, message,
details}`.

JobFailureCode.title: JobFailureCode
JobFailureCode.description:
The codes a job fails with that no refusal carries. A job's
`error.code` is a refusal code (`refusals.RefusalCode`: what
stopped it was a refusal, or `internal_error`) or one of these.
`tests/test_openapi_schema.py` fails when a job or a job's stream
fails with a code in neither list.

JobList.title: JobList
JobList.description:
Every job the sidecar remembers: running ones, and finished ones
for a few minutes.

KeptBackup.title: KeptBackup
KeptBackup.description:
The Backup that keeps the Workbench a Restore or a reset to Live
replaced.

LabelRemoved.title: LabelRemoved
LabelRemoved.description:
The message's stored Label is gone (`deleted` is false when it
had none); the rules, or nobody, decide it again.

LabelSet.title: LabelSet
LabelSet.description: The user's Label as stored, with the verdict it replaced.

LabelStats.title: LabelStats
LabelStats.description: How a conversation's messages resolve, its alias group included.

LabelledMessage.title: LabelledMessage
LabelledMessage.description:
A message with the Label it resolves to (null for a system line)
and its `hash`, which the Label routes take. `label_source` and the
rest are there only when a stored Label decides it: who set it, the
reason given, and the verdict it replaced.

LabelsCleared.title: LabelsCleared
LabelsCleared.description:
One conversation's Labels went to the Trash as `trash_id` (null
when there were none).

LabelsOverridden.title: LabelsOverridden
LabelsOverridden.description:
`label` as the request gave it; `changed` counts the Labels
written or removed.

LabelsRollup.title: LabelsRollup
LabelsRollup.description:
Counts across every conversation of every character, and how
many Labels the user set by hand.

LabelsSettings.title: LabelsSettings
LabelsSettings.description:
Messages shorter than `threshold_chars` are OOC without asking
anyone. The defaults let the window show "(default)" hints and offer
a reset without hardcoding them.

LexicalRebuilt.title: LexicalRebuilt
LexicalRebuilt.description: How many chunks the lexical half of the Index now holds.

Live.title: Live
Live.description:
A character's Live: F-list's character-data answer as the last
Pull stored it, plus `fetched_at`. Free-form, because F-list may add
fields and the window passes on what it does not know.

LogCharacter.title: LogCharacter
LogCharacter.description:
One of the user's characters with Logs. `mtime`: the newest
change in its Logs folder (epoch seconds), 0 when it has none.

LogContact.title: LogContact
LogContact.description: One of the user's characters with a 1-on-1 Log with the name.

LogPartner.title: LogPartner

LogSearchAllNothing.title: LogSearchAllNothing
LogSearchAllNothing.description: What a search of every conversation answers for an empty query.

LogSearchHit.title: LogSearchHit
LogSearchHit.description:
A message that matches a search, with its `index` in its
conversation. (Bases in this order put `index` first, as the
answer has it.)

LogSearchPartner.title: LogSearchPartner
LogSearchPartner.description:
One conversation's matches; `truncated` when it had more than
the limit (open the conversation to see the rest).

MappingList.title: MappingList
MappingList.description:
F-list's mapping list (kinks, infotags and their groups, list
items) as F-list sent it, then two keys of the sidecar's: the
cached file's sha256 (`_etag`) and when it was fetched
(`_fetched_at`, unix seconds).

McpAuth.title: McpAuth
McpAuth.description: The optional bearer token for the MCP endpoints; off by default.

McpEndpoint.title: McpEndpoint

McpSettings.title: McpSettings
McpSettings.description:
MCP settings only the window may change. `log_text`: whether MCP
clients get the tools that return Log text; off by default.

PairingHandshake.title: PairingHandshake
PairingHandshake.description:
A pairing the extension started: it keeps `token` and polls the
handshake's status until the window accepts it.

PartnerLabelStats.title: PartnerLabelStats
PartnerLabelStats.description:
`LabelStats` of one conversation in a character's list.
`log_mtime` (the newest of the group's Logs) later than
`last_label_at` (its newest Label) means messages arrived that no
one has judged yet. Both epoch seconds, null when there is none.

PendingHandshake.title: PendingHandshake
PendingHandshake.description:
A pairing waiting for the window's accept. `fingerprint` is a
short form of the token, for the user to compare.

PendingRender.title: PendingRender
PendingRender.description:
Something a tool asked the app to draw: BBCode, the inline
images it names, the preview theme and the width in pixels.
`label` is for the app's log line only.

PoolImage.title: PoolImage
PoolImage.description: An image file in the character's Pool.

PreUploadBackupKept.title: PreUploadBackupKept
PreUploadBackupKept.description:
The Backup taken before an Upload; `snapshot_id` is the
extension's name for its file name.

PublicProfile.title: PublicProfile
PublicProfile.description:
A character's public profile, for the editor's "Fetch profile".
`stats` are its infotags by label; `inlines` F-list's inline images
by id, as F-list sent them.

PullDone.description:
A Pull ended: `changed` whether F-list's profile differed from
Live, and the images by outcome.
PullDone.title: PullDone

PullEvents.description:
A Pull's events, in the order a Pull sends them: the job, then
its progress, ending with `done`, `error` or `cancelled`.
PullEvents.title: PullEvents

PullFetching.description: A Pull is asking F-list for the character.
PullFetching.title: PullFetching

PullImage.description:
One image of a Pull: kept (`cached`: it was on disk already) or
not (`error` says why).
PullImage.title: PullImage

PullImages.description: A Pull's images start: how many the profile lists.
PullImages.title: PullImages

PullStatus.title: PullStatus
PullStatus.description: Whether a character's last Pull got every image.

PullTicket.description: A Pull is getting (or refreshing) the F-list ticket. No data.
PullTicket.title: PullTicket

PutBackImage.title: PutBackImage
PutBackImage.description:
An image back in the Pool. `deduplicated`: the Pool already held
these bytes (under `image_id`), so the Trash's copy was dropped.

PutBackLabels.title: PutBackLabels
PutBackLabels.description:
One cleared-Labels entry put back. A message labelled again
since keeps its newer Label; its hash is under `skipped`.

RagValues.title: RagValues
RagValues.description: The Index and retrieval tunables, as set or as their defaults.

RefusalBody.title: RefusalBody
RefusalBody.description:
What every route answers when it is not ok, as the schema
declares it (`REFUSAL_RESPONSES`). `Refusal.body()` and server.py's
handlers build the dict; this only describes it.

RefusalCode.title: RefusalCode
RefusalCode.description:
Every `code` a REST refusal can carry. The OpenAPI schema lists
them, so the window's `RefusalCode` is a generated union and a
switch on a code the sidecar never answers fails the type-check.

A class below names its code where it is defined; this list repeats
it for the schema. `tests/test_openapi_schema.py` fails when a
`Refusal` subclass carries a code missing here (its `code`, or the
keys of `STATUS_BY_CODE` / `CODES` for classes coded per instance).

RenderFailedRequest.title: RenderFailedRequest
RenderFailedRequest.description:
Why the app could not draw a picture; without one the caller
hears a general reason.

RestorePreflight.title: RestorePreflight
RestorePreflight.description:
What the Restore confirm dialog says: whether the Workbench holds
edits, and whether Live was pulled after the Backup was taken.

RestoreRequest.title: RestoreRequest
RestoreRequest.description:
Restore a Backup into the Workbench.

`back_up_first` is still accepted from older windows and ignored:
the Workbench is always kept as a Backup first (ADR 0003).

RosterEntry.title: RosterEntry
RosterEntry.description:
A character the picker lists: on the account, kept in the app, or
with Logs, and which of those.

Settings.title: Settings
Settings.description: The settings the sidecar keeps, as Settings shows them.

StreamError.description:
A stream's `error` event, which ends it: the stage it stopped
at, then the one error shape `{code, message, details}`.
StreamError.title: StreamError

StreamReady.description: The stream is live: its first event.
StreamReady.title: StreamReady

Trash.title: Trash
Trash.description: A character's Trash: images, Backups and cleared Labels.

TrashItem.title: TrashItem
TrashItem.description: An image file in a character's Trash.

TrashPurged.title: TrashPurged
TrashPurged.description: What was deleted for good from the Trash, by the id it had there.

TrashedBackup.title: TrashedBackup
TrashedBackup.description: A deleted Backup in a character's Trash.

TrashedImage.title: TrashedImage
TrashedImage.description: An image just moved into the Trash.

TrashedLabels.title: TrashedLabels
TrashedLabels.description: Labels cleared in one go, kept in the Trash.

UnlabeledFilled.title: UnlabeledFilled
UnlabeledFilled.description:
`hashes` is exactly what was written, which
`/labels/delete-hashes` takes to undo it.

UploadCharacter.title: UploadCharacter
UploadCharacter.description: An archived character the extension can take Upload sources from.

UploadSourceBackup.title: UploadSourceBackup
UploadSourceBackup.description:
A Backup as an Upload source. `kind` "pre-restore" is the
extension's name for a Backup taken before an Upload; `backup_kind`
is the Backup list's `kind`. `upload_refused` says why it cannot be
uploaded, or is null.

UploadSourceWorkbench.title: UploadSourceWorkbench
UploadSourceWorkbench.description:
The Workbench as an Upload source. `kind` is "set" because
extension 0.1.1 finds the Workbench by it.

UploadedImage.title: UploadedImage
UploadedImage.description:
The Pool image an upload landed as. `deduplicated`: the Pool
already held these bytes, and this is that file.

WorkbenchAbsent.title: WorkbenchAbsent
WorkbenchAbsent.description:
No Workbench yet. `no_live`: the character was never pulled, so
there is nothing to copy from; `not_created_yet`: nobody has edited
it yet.

WorkbenchInfo.title: WorkbenchInfo
WorkbenchInfo.description: When the Workbench was made and last saved (unix seconds).

WorkbenchPayload.title: WorkbenchPayload
WorkbenchPayload.description:
The Workbench payload and the etag a save sends back as
`If-Match`. `created`: this read made it from Live.

WorkbenchSaveRequest.title: WorkbenchSaveRequest
WorkbenchSaveRequest.description:
The whole Workbench payload a save writes: F-list's
character-data shape plus the app's `_schema_version` and
`_overlay`. Free-form, because F-list may add fields and the
Workbench keeps what it does not know.
